---
title: "Prepare NYC dog names"
execute:
  echo: true
  message: false
---

Count and exclude licenses with missing names or unusable birth years, then prepare one row per estimated dog from the 2024 NYC licenses.

## Packages and helpers
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
source("helpers.R")
```

## Read the license records
Read the fields as text so ZIPs remain identifiers and recorded birth years can be inspected before conversion. The source uses six labels for missing names. `na = missing_name_labels` reads all six as R missing values so they receive the same treatment. The saved source CSV retains the recorded labels.

Keep ZIP strings as supplied. In this snapshot, all dogs selected for the NYC income comparison already have five-digit ZIPs. The 40 named-license records with short ZIPs are outside that comparison, so restoring their zeros would not change the selected dogs.
```{r}
#| label: read-license-records
missing_name_labels <- c(
  "UNKNOWN", "NAME NOT PROVIDED", "NONE", "NA", ".", "NONAME"
)

sources <- read_csv("data/sources.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
dogs_raw <- read_csv(
  "data/raw/nyc-dogs-2024.csv",
  col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
  na = missing_name_labels, trim_ws = FALSE
)
```

## Give the license fields clear names
Give the city's columns clear working names. This changes the headings without changing their values.
```{r}
#| label: name-license-columns
dogs_raw |>
  rename(
    name = animalname,
    sex = animalgender,
    birth_year = animalbirth,
    breed = breedname,
    license_issue_date = licenseissueddate,
    license_expiry_date = licenseexpireddate
  ) ->
  licenses_renamed
```

## Number the source records
Number the licenses before filtering or sorting. `source_row_id` lets us find each recorded license in the saved CSV after later transformations. `row_number()` assigns 1, 2, 3 and so on in the current row order.
```{r}
#| label: number-source-records
licenses_renamed |>
  mutate(source_row_id = row_number()) ->
  licenses

licenses |>
  preview()
```

## Count and exclude missing names
The six source labels have already become missing values during import. `is.na()` answers TRUE for a missing name and FALSE for a recorded name. Keep those answers in source-row order for counting and filtering.
```{r}
#| label: identify-missing-names
licenses |>
  pull(name) |>
  is.na() ->
  name_missing
```

Report missing names by ZIP before excluding them. The temporary `name_missing` column is used only for this summary. `sum()` counts TRUE answers; dividing by all licenses in the ZIP gives the missing-name share. ZIPs are grouped using their recorded text.
```{r}
#| label: summarize-missingness-by-zip
licenses |>
  mutate(name_missing = name_missing) |>
  group_by(extract_year, zipcode) |>
  summarise(
    source_license_records = n(),
    missing_name_records = sum(name_missing),
    named_license_records = source_license_records - missing_name_records,
    missing_name_share = missing_name_records / source_license_records,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(extract_year = as.integer(extract_year)) |>
  arrange(zipcode) ->
  missing_by_zip

licenses |>
  filter(!name_missing) ->
  named_licenses
```

## Count and exclude unusable birth years
Keep recorded years from 1990 through 2024. `1990:2024` makes that sequence, and `as.character()` writes the years as text to match the imported column. Membership in this list also requires the four-digit spelling. Count the rejected years, preserve those licenses in an exclusion report, and continue with the usable records.

The optional [birth-year inference reference](birth-year-inferences.qmd) preserves six considered corrections and the operation that applied them. Exclusion gives us one consistent rule without guessing a birth year.
```{r}
#| label: exclude-unusable-birth-years
# Count and exclude records with unusable birth years. Keeping the six inferred corrections would change any existing chart share by at most 0.007 percentage points; see birth-year-inferences.qmd.
usable_birth_years <- as.character(1990:2024)

named_licenses |>
  pull(birth_year) |>
  is.element(usable_birth_years) ->
  birth_year_usable

named_licenses |>
  filter(!birth_year_usable) ->
  excluded_birth_year_licenses

excluded_birth_year_licenses |>
  count(birth_year, name = "source_license_records", sort = TRUE) ->
  birth_year_exclusion_counts

birth_year_exclusion_counts

named_licenses |>
  filter(birth_year_usable) ->
  usable_licenses
```

This excludes 45 named licenses before name formatting, date conversion or dog grouping. Together with the 5,810 missing-name exclusions, it leaves 100,119 licenses for preparation.

## Record the remaining cleaning details
Identify compound names before removing their separators, and record unknown breeds for the cleaning report. These report fields do not cause exclusions or appear in the exported dog tables. Unknown breeds remain as recorded. There are no missing ZIPs in this snapshot, so there is no missing-ZIP filter.
```{r}
#| label: prepare-cleaning-report-fields
usable_licenses |>
  mutate(breed_label = str_trim(breed)) |>
  mutate(breed_label = str_to_upper(breed_label)) |>
  mutate(
    compound_name = str_detect(name, "\\S\\s+\\S|[^\\s-]-[^\\s-]"),
    breed_unknown = is.element(breed_label, c("", "UNKNOWN"))
  ) |>
  select(-breed_label) ->
  licenses_for_formatting
```

## Format names for matching
Uppercase the whole name, then remove spaces and hyphens. These are the spelling differences we agreed to ignore when matching. For example, `WALL-E` becomes `WALLE`. The compound-name report field already records whether the unmodified name contained separators.
```{r}
#| label: format-names
licenses_for_formatting |>
  mutate(name = str_to_upper(name, locale = "en")) |>
  mutate(name = str_remove_all(name, "[\\s-]")) ->
  licenses_with_matching_names
```

## Read license dates
The source dates include a time. Take the first ten characters, such as `2024-05-30`, and read them as dates so we can sort the licenses.
```{r}
#| label: read-license-dates
licenses_with_matching_names |>
  mutate(
    license_issue_date = str_sub(license_issue_date, 1, 10),
    license_expiry_date = str_sub(license_expiry_date, 1, 10)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    license_issue_date = parse_date(license_issue_date),
    license_expiry_date = parse_date(license_expiry_date),
    extract_year = as.integer(extract_year)
  ) ->
  licenses_with_dates

licenses_with_dates |>
  select(source_row_id, name, zipcode, birth_year, license_issue_date) |>
  preview()
```

## Estimate individual dogs
We treat licenses with the same full name after formatting, sex, birth year, breed and ZIP as one estimated dog. Within each group, sort the newest issue date first. A tie goes to the later expiry date, then to the earlier source row. `slice_head(n = 1)` keeps the first license in each sorted group. `license_record_count` records how many licenses that row represents. For example, the two matching TOTORO licenses were issued in 2019 and 2024. The 2024 row represents both.
```{r}
#| label: estimate-individual-dogs
dog_key <- c("name", "sex", "birth_year", "breed", "zipcode")
licenses_with_dates |>
  group_by(name, sex, birth_year, breed, zipcode) |>
  mutate(
    license_record_count = n(),
    latest_issue_date = max(license_issue_date),
    latest_issue_ties = sum(license_issue_date == latest_issue_date)
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(license_issue_date), desc(license_expiry_date), source_row_id, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n = 1) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    retained_row_label = str_pad(source_row_id, width = 6, pad = "0"),
    estimated_dog_id = str_c("dog2024-", retained_row_label)
  ) |>
  arrange(source_row_id) ->
  dogs_estimated

dogs_estimated |>
  select(estimated_dog_id, name, license_record_count) |>
  preview()
```

## Keep the dog fields
Pass the working fields to analysis. The source row number links each dog to its recorded values. Leave report fields out of this table.
```{r}
#| label: select-dog-fields
dogs_estimated |>
  select(
    estimated_dog_id, source_row_id, extract_year, name,
    sex, birth_year, breed, zipcode,
    license_issue_date, license_expiry_date, license_record_count
  ) ->
  dogs_prepared
```

## Trace source records to dogs
Map the usable licenses to their retained dog row. Keep every source row in the audit, including the early exclusions. Excluded licenses have their source row and reason, but no dog ID because they do not enter grouping.
```{r}
#| label: trace-source-records-to-dogs
dogs_prepared |>
  select(all_of(dog_key), estimated_dog_id, retained_source_row_id = source_row_id) ->
  dog_identity_lookup

licenses_with_dates |>
  left_join(dog_identity_lookup, by = dog_key) |>
  select(source_row_id, estimated_dog_id, retained_source_row_id) ->
  usable_license_mapping

excluded_birth_year_licenses |>
  pull(source_row_id) ->
  excluded_birth_year_source_rows

licenses |>
  select(source_row_id) |>
  left_join(usable_license_mapping, by = "source_row_id") |>
  mutate(
    record_status = case_when(
      is.element(source_row_id, excluded_birth_year_source_rows) ~ "excluded_birth_year",
      is.na(estimated_dog_id) ~ "missing_name",
      source_row_id == retained_source_row_id ~ "retained",
      TRUE ~ "consolidated"
    )
  ) ->
  license_audit
```

## Cleaning summary
The source uses six labels for missing names: `UNKNOWN`, `NAME NOT PROVIDED`, `NONE`, `NA`, `.`, and `NONAME`. The report combines them into one missing-name count across all source licenses and also reports missingness by recorded ZIP; it does not distinguish which label was used. Formatting and breed findings describe the usable licenses and their estimated dogs. The birth-year exclusion count describes the 45 named licenses removed before grouping. The separate exclusion CSV preserves their recorded fields for inspection.
```{r}
#| label: summarize-cleaning
missing_by_zip |>
  summarise(
    source_license_records = sum(source_license_records),
    missing_name_records = sum(missing_name_records),
    missing_name_share = missing_name_records / source_license_records
  )

quality_flags <- c("breed_unknown", "compound_name")
licenses_with_dates |>
  summarise(across(all_of(quality_flags), sum)) |>
  mutate(unit = "named_license_record") ->
  license_quality_counts

dogs_estimated |>
  summarise(across(all_of(quality_flags), sum)) |>
  mutate(unit = "estimated_dog") ->
  dog_quality_counts

dogs_estimated |>
  filter(latest_issue_ties > 1) |>
  summarise(unit = "estimated_dog", flag = "latest_issue_ties", count = n()) ->
  latest_issue_tie_count

excluded_birth_year_licenses |>
  summarise(unit = "named_license_record", flag = "excluded_birth_year", count = n()) ->
  birth_year_exclusion_total

license_quality_counts |>
  bind_rows(dog_quality_counts) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(quality_flags), names_to = "flag", values_to = "count") |>
  select(unit, flag, count) |>
  bind_rows(latest_issue_tie_count, birth_year_exclusion_total) ->
  quality_summary

quality_summary
```

## Save the prepared dogs
```{r}
#| label: save-dogs
# Create the folder for these tables if needed.
dir.create("data/derived", showWarnings = FALSE)
write_csv(dogs_prepared, "data/derived/dogs_prepared_2024.csv", na = "")
write_csv(license_audit, "data/derived/license_to_dog.csv", na = "")
write_csv(missing_by_zip, "data/derived/missing_names_by_zip.csv", na = "")
write_csv(excluded_birth_year_licenses, "data/derived/excluded_birth_year_licenses.csv", na = "")
write_csv(quality_summary, "data/derived/quality_flags.csv", na = "")
```

Different dogs can share all five identifying fields. A change in a dog's recorded details can also split its licenses into several groups. These are estimates of individual dogs.
